laws.rule: In the land core of the Calanques National Park (the walking area around Marseille and Cassis), the park lists as prohibited: smoking or lighting a fire, including at the water's edge and including barbecues and camp stoves; bivouacking, camping and caravanning; and picking flowers, damaging trees or taking species. Dogs must be on a lead.
laws.heading: Parc national des Calanques, good practice and regulations (land core)

laws.rule: Flying a drone or model aircraft is prohibited in both the land core and the marine core of the Calanques National Park.
laws.heading: Parc national des Calanques, good practice and regulations

laws.rule: In the marine core of the Calanques National Park, sailing, anchoring or landing in the restricted zones is prohibited, as is taking protected species or underwater cultural property. A 5-knot speed limit applies within 300 metres of the coast.
laws.heading: Parc national des Calanques, good practice and regulations (sea)

laws.rule: The park runs a reservation system for the Sugiton calanque (a cove near Marseille) in summer; the park's own Sugiton reservation page is the place to book and to check the season's dates, which are set each year. The park page's rules text was not readable in full on 6 November 2026, so the dates and quota are not stated here.
laws.heading: Parc national des Calanques, Réservation Sugiton

laws.rule: Mercantour National Park core (Alpes-Maritimes and Alpes-de-Haute-Provence): camping is prohibited. Bivouac is allowed only from 19:00 to 09:00 and more than one hour's walk inside the park boundary or from the last road access; sleeping in a camper van, caravan or roof tent is prohibited. Fires are prohibited in general; a hiking stove is allowed within the prefecture's fire-prevention orders. Dogs are banned even on a lead or carried, with limited exceptions such as dogs of residents of hamlets reachable by road.
laws.heading: Parc national du Mercantour, La réglementation (camping, feu, chiens)

laws.rule: Mercantour National Park core: leisure drones are prohibited. Motorised flight below 1,000 m above the ground is prohibited, and activities that fly low over the core with a sail or wing (base-jumping, speed-riding, wingsuit) are prohibited.
laws.heading: Parc national du Mercantour, Les drones de loisir en cœur de Parc national; La réglementation

laws.rule: Mercantour National Park core: taking minerals, fossils, plants or animals is prohibited, with a limited list of plants allowed for picking under a separate park order. Noise that disturbs the calm, including speakers and radios, is prohibited, as are graffiti and leaving rubbish. Diving is prohibited, and so is navigation by boat, paddleboard or kayak. Canyoning is prohibited. Motor vehicles are prohibited except on a short list of named roads and tracks.
laws.heading: Parc national du Mercantour, La réglementation

laws.rule: Port-Cros National Park (Hyères islands, Var): in the protected natural areas of Port-Cros and Porquerolles, camping and bivouac are prohibited. Fires and smoking are not allowed outside the Port-Cros village. Dogs must be on a lead on paths and are not allowed on beaches; on Port-Cros they are allowed on a lead only in the village between the Fort du Moulin and the statue of Saint-Joseph. Guide and assistance dogs are not covered.
laws.heading: Parc national de Port-Cros, La réglementation

laws.rule: Port-Cros National Park cores (Port-Cros island and islets, and the beaches and natural areas of Porquerolles): flying over the cores is prohibited for any aircraft, including leisure drones (article 15 of decree 2009-449), unless the park director authorises it. Professional or commercial filming and sound recording in the cores needs park authorisation.
laws.heading: Parc national de Port-Cros, Réglementation survol

laws.rule: Port-Cros National Park: the marine cores are a strip of sea out to 600 metres from the coast around Port-Cros and Porquerolles. Boat movement, anchoring and diving there are controlled by prefectural orders (2023-116 for Porquerolles, 2023-117 for Port-Cros) with maps on the park's site; recreational fishing is regulated in the marine cores and the adjacent maritime area. Read the park's maps before anchoring or diving. Take nothing from the natural environment and stay on the paths.
laws.heading: Parc national de Port-Cros, Navigation plaisance; La réglementation

laws.rule: Var department: each summer the prefecture regulates entry, driving and parking on routes serving the 9 forest massifs (Centre Var, Corniche des Maures, Estérel, Haut Var, Îles d'Hyères, Maures, Monts Toulonnais, Plateau de Canjuers, Sainte-Baume). A map is published every day before 19:00 for the next day, from mid-June to the end of September; in 2026 it ran from 8 June to 30 September. The rules rest on the prefectoral order of 19 June 2018, amended by the order of 10 July 2020. On Very Severe and Extreme risk days, access is closed on the listed roads; the few approved forest reception sites (ZAPEF) can stay open on Very Severe days but not on Extreme days. Roads with a B0 sign are closed to vehicles whatever the risk level. Estérel risk levels also apply to the western massifs of Alpes-Maritimes.
laws.heading: Préfecture du Var, Carte d'accès aux massifs du Var (arrêtés préfectoraux du 19 juin 2018 et du 10 juillet 2020)

laws.rule: Var department: the prefectoral order of 2 November 2025 on use of fire bans all fire use from 1 June to 30 September. Within or less than 200 metres from a forest, the public may not carry or light open flames, and may not throw lit items such as cigarette butts into forests or onto roads through them (fourth-class contravention, a fine category in French law). Outside that period a ban also applies on days when the wind is above 40 km/h. Burning garden waste in the open is banned all year across the department (third-class contravention).
laws.heading: Préfecture du Var, Emploi du feu: arrêté préfectoral du 2 novembre 2025

laws.rule: Bouches-du-Rhône department: from 1 June to 30 September, access, presence and movement in the forest massifs (including the Calanques area) is regulated by prefectoral order of 22 April 2025, partly revised by the order of 9 July 2026 (no. AP-2026-13-2026-07-09-00020). Access for each massif is set daily from Météo-France weather and dryness data and published as a map around 18:00 for the next day. The prefecture lists smoking, camp fires and barbecues among the banned acts. It describes the department as the most exposed to forest fire in mainland France.
laws.heading: Préfecture des Bouches-du-Rhône, Accès et travaux dans les massifs forestiers (arrêté du 22 avril 2025, révisé le 9 juillet 2026)

laws.rule: Alpes-Maritimes department: prefectoral order no. 2025-101 of 13 May 2025 sets summer rules for the forest massifs (forests, scrub and maquis, including paths and tracks through them). In the summer period, at any risk level, smoking and throwing butts are banned, fires and barbecues are banned, and driving or parking on forest tracks is banned except for those with rights of access. Access then depends on a daily Météo-France risk map by commune: green, access allowed; yellow and orange, access advised against; red, access banned all day. The 2026 daily map started Monday 8 June 2026 at 18:00. From 1 June to 30 September all burning is banned and carrying equipment that could start a fire is restricted. Portable hiking stoves are tolerated only in set conditions: outside that period on flat ground cleared of vegetation within 3 metres; inside it only at green risk level (on equipped bivouac areas in massifs of class 1 and 2).
laws.heading: Préfecture des Alpes-Maritimes, arrêté 2025-101 du 13 mai 2025 and its summary sheets

laws.rule: Vaucluse department: from 15 June to 15 September access to the forest massifs and work in sensitive areas can be limited or banned depending on weather. Risk 'Rouge E' (extreme): no access. Risk 'Rouge': access banned all day except at listed exempt sites (for example the Cedar Forest of the Petit Luberon trail, the Sentier des ocres at Roussillon and the Colorado Provençal at Rustrel). Yellow: allowed, morning advised. Green: allowed. The map is published each day before 19:00 for the next day. Basis: prefectoral order of 29 March 2023 on access to massifs, with the 2026 list of exempt sites set by order of 16 July 2026.
laws.heading: Préfecture de Vaucluse, Réglementation de l'accès aux massifs forestiers (arrêté du 29 mars 2023; sites dérogatoires 2026)

laws.rule: Var department drought rules: the framework order (arrêté-cadre) of 1 July 2025 sets levels (vigilance, alert, reinforced alert, crisis) with limits on water use. In 2026 the prefecture put 12 communes at reinforced alert, 90 at alert and 51 at vigilance, and none at crisis. The prefecture page updated 13 October 2026 says the restrictions have been lifted, and asks for continued restraint in watering gardens, washing vehicles and filling pools. The national VigiEau site shows which limits apply in a given commune.
laws.heading: Préfecture du Var, Point de situation sécheresse 2026; arrêté-cadre du 1er juillet 2025

laws.rule: Bouches-du-Rhône department drought rules: the prefecture's table for households (22 July 2025) lists limits by level. Washing a vehicle at home is banned at alert, reinforced alert and crisis levels. Filling a private pool over 1 cubic metre is banned at alert level where the supply is local water (topping up allowed if first filled before the restrictions began) and banned at crisis level. Lawn watering is limited to outside 09:00 to 19:00 at alert level and banned at reinforced alert. On 25 September 2026 the Huveaune sector was at alert, the Arc (upper and lower) and Réal-de-Jouques sectors at reinforced alert, and the rest of the department at vigilance. The prefecture page names no framework order number.
laws.heading: Préfecture des Bouches-du-Rhône, Les mesures de restriction de l'usage de l'eau (tableaux particuliers) and Point de situation du 25 septembre 2026

layers.process: In the park cores, public events, professional or commercial filming and sound recording, motorised flight, and collecting from the natural environment can't go ahead without the park's prior authorisation. Anchoring and diving in the marine cores follow prefectural orders and maps published by the park.
In the park core, a group of more than 10 riding or pack animals needs the park's authorisation, and bivouac is limited to the hours and distances set by the park. Leisure drones are not allowed.

sources.title: Les drones de loisir en cœur de Parc national
